questions.text: Which of the following statements correctly describe the learned reverse process in a DDPM?
options: The reverse process is parameterized by a neural network that predicts the noise component at a given timestep.
The reverse process gradually transforms a noisy sample into a sample resembling the data distribution.
The reverse process is completely fixed once the forward noise schedule is chosen.
The neural network is trained to predict the class label of the original clean sample.
Each reverse step is deterministic and does not involve any randomness.
correct_answer: The reverse process is parameterized by a neural network that predicts the noise component at a given timestep.
The reverse process gradually transforms a noisy sample into a sample resembling the data distribution.

questions.text: Which among the following about DDPM and DDIM are correct?
options: Both DDPM and DDIM require simulating a Markov chain for many steps in order to produce a sample.
Both DDPM and DDIM follow the same process for training.
DDIM produces higher-quality samples than DDPM only when the number of sampling steps is very large.

DDIM re-trains only the final layer of the DDPM network.
correct_answer: Both DDPM and DDIM follow the same process for training.
The objective function for both DDPM and DDIM are same.
